sourceLevel.valueLabel: Level this app gives the audio of {{process}}, in percent
sourceLevel.hint: Level applied to this program's audio on its copies: 100 leaves it as produced, below attenuates, above amplifies; copies only, never the device Windows plays. Drag, or step {{step}}% at a time with the wheel / arrow keys (Shift for ×10); click to type a value

deviceLatency.reading: Measured {{ms}} ms — the software side only; what a codec or a Bluetooth link adds cannot be seen from user mode

deviceVolume.valueLabel: Volume of {{device}}, relative to the loudest device

calibration.title: Calibrate delays
calibration.intro: Pick the devices to calibrate (at least two). They take turns playing a short tone, one burst each per round: tap the button once for every tone you hear — too early or too late does not count. Once everything is measured the compensation is computed for you, and the slowest device becomes the alignment baseline.
calibration.tap: Tap when you hear a tone
calibration.sloppy: That tap answered no tone, so it does not count — tap on the next one
calibration.noPresses: No tap was counted for {{devices}}. Wait for the tone to sound before tapping.
calibration.baselineNote: Aligned on {{name}} — it keeps compensation 0, and every other device is held back to meet it. When routing, make the baseline the first device (the primary output).
calibration.rebaseHint: Tap any row to re-pick the baseline — the numbers are recomputed, nothing is measured again.
calibration.laggingBehind: {{device}} measured about {{slow}} ms slower than the baseline: software delay can only hold sound back, never make it earlier, so this one cannot catch up — it will stay about {{late}} ms behind the baseline.
calibration.laggingClose: {{device}} differs from the baseline by only {{diff}} ms, less than the engine's base pipeline (100 ms): it cannot fully align. Written as 0, it will stay about {{late}} ms behind the baseline.
calibration.applyFailed: Not every value was written; retry, or check the per-device list below by hand.
calibration.finetune: The engine's base pipeline is already accounted for; if it still sounds off by a hair, nudge the values on the board's tuning strip.

primaryVolume.hint: The program's own session volume: only this path drops, and the copies are compensated. It floors at 5% — to mute this device while the copies play on, make another device primary and turn this one down as a copy

stage.guide: Select an app on the left
stage.primaryTitle: Windows plays this device directly, so there is no delay to compensate; volume is the program's own session volume, so only this path drops and the copies are compensated
stage.promoteTitle: Let the system play this device directly; the others become its copies
stage.changePrimaryTitle: Pick the device Windows plays directly; the others stay copies
stage.groupCopiesEmpty: No copy and no app input yet
stage.addTargetTitle: Play through another device, or into another app's input
stage.feedTitleSuspended: Not moving: {{source}}'s route holds the output slot; stop it and the feed resumes
stage.feedTitleNoCarrier: Not moving: no carrier set — pick a loopback pair in Settings → Feed carrier
stage.stripPrimaryNote: This is the program's session volume — only the main path changes; the copies are compensated.
stage.stripPrimaryLatency: The primary is played by Windows directly, so there is no measured latency to show here.

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoRememberDesc: Remember each program's device routing and restore it automatically
settings.resetEndpointsDesc: Frees a program that no longer follows the system's playback device; routed programs are untouched
settings.stopAllRoutesDesc: Returns every routed program to the system default at once; unrouted programs are untouched.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: On: closing tucks the window into the tray and routes keep running. Off: closing quits the app and stops them.
settings.autostartDesc: Launches silently into the tray at sign-in; remembered routes are ready before you open anything
settings.delayNote: Delay is per device: here, on the rows below, or in the tuning strip of a copy picked on the board. It applies only when one program goes to several devices — a single-device route is played by the system directly.
settings.delayCalibrateDesc: Plays short tones on each device in turn — tap the moment you hear one, three times per device. Each copy's compensation is written from the measured difference; nothing is guessed from the device's type.
settings.delayCalibrateNeedsTwo: Needs two output devices: one to hear first, one to catch up with.
settings.delayStepDesc: How much each − / + click changes; an exact value can also be typed
settings.calibrationNote: What is measured is the difference in when you hear the tone; your own reaction is the same on every device and cancels out. If it is still a hair off, nudge it on the tuning strip.
settings.sourceLevelsAlignDesc: Brings every duplicating program that is playing up to the loudest one's level
settings.sourceLevelsNote: A program on several devices wears its level as the dial under its card on the board. The level is the gain this app applies to its own copy; the program's own volume and what Windows stores are untouched, and 100 leaves it as produced.
settings.feedCarrierDesc: A feed goes through a loopback pair: the source plays to the pair's playback side, the target records from its recording side. Pick a pair from a loopback driver (such as VB-Cable); without one, feeds are remembered but stay silent.
settings.feedCarrierRenderHint: The pair's playback endpoint, often named “… Input”
settings.feedCarrierCaptureHint: The pair's recording endpoint, often named “… Output”
settings.feedCarrierDetected: Found {{driver}} — both sides are on the lists
settings.feedCarrierMissing: No loopback driver found. A free VB-Cable is enough — the lists here refresh on their own, no restart needed.
settings.feedCarrierDownloadFailed: The browser did not open — copy the address of the VB-Cable page and open it yourself.
settings.replayTourDesc: The guide that runs the first time a version starts on this PC — what the board is, what feeding another program needs, and the two background habits. It is answered once and never comes back on its own.
settings.helpDesc: The README covers the board, the loopback pair a feed runs through, and what Windows keeps after this app closes. It opens in your browser.
settings.helpFailed: The browser did not open — the documentation lives in this app's repository.
settings.aboutDesc: Per-app audio routing for Windows — Rust on Core Audio directly, with no helper process and no driver bundled. Feeds run through a loopback endpoint pair you install and pick yourself.

startup.upgradeTitle: An earlier version ran on this PC
startup.upgradeBody: It may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you encounter this, clear it with the button below; otherwise no action is needed.
startup.upgradeBodyVersion: The last version to run on this PC was {{version}}, and it may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you encounter this, clear it with the button below; otherwise no action is needed.
startup.resetHint: This clears every program that is running now, including a device you set by hand in the volume mixer. A program that is not running keeps its device until it starts.
startup.resetDone: Cleared the fixed output device of {{n}} program(s).
startup.resetRemaining: {{processes}} could not be cleared — a program must be playing audio to be released; try again.

wizard.welcomeBody: This is a per-app audio router: each program's sound goes where you send it, while everything else keeps following the system default. Windows cannot do this on its own — that is the whole point of the app.
wizard.welcomePoint1: Route any program to any output device — or to several at once
wizard.welcomePoint2: Feed one program's audio into another program's microphone input
wizard.welcomePoint3: Everything is remembered: routes and feeds come back with the program
wizard.boardBody: The program you select sits in the middle. Its destinations line up on the right — output devices first, then programs receiving its sound. A line from the program to a destination is the route itself, and the number on a card is its place in that order.
wizard.boardPoint1: Click a destination row to connect it or let it go; ＋ in the panel's title row adds another device, or another program's input
wizard.boardPoint2: Nothing changes until you click the program card — the board proposes first, applies on your word
wizard.boardPoint3: Click the number leading a row to tune that destination — delay and share for a copy, the program's own volume for the main one
wizard.carrierBody: Sending sound into a program's microphone runs through a loopback driver's endpoint pair. The app ships no driver and installs none — one you already have is recognized here, and the free VB-Cable's own page opens from the button below. Skipping this costs nothing else: routing to devices works without it.
wizard.carrierMissing: No loopback driver found. Install the free VB-Cable now, or pick the pair later in Settings → Feed carrier.
wizard.backgroundBody: The app lives in the tray and keeps routes working with the window closed. Two habits to choose:
wizard.backgroundAutostartHint: Starts hidden in the tray, so remembered routes are already in place when you sign in.
wizard.backgroundCloseToTray: Closing the window only tucks it away
wizard.backgroundCloseToTrayHint: Otherwise the X exits the app and stops every route.
wizard.inheritBody: This computer ran the app before. The routes and feeds it remembered, the delay compensation, device shares and program levels are all still here: keep them, or clear them and start clean.
wizard.inheritBodyVersion: Last run here was {{version}}. The routes and feeds it remembered, the delay compensation, device shares and program levels are all still here: keep them, or clear them and start clean.
wizard.inheritKeepHint: Everything stays as it is: remembered routes and feeds, delay compensation, device shares and program levels.
wizard.inheritCleanHint: Remembered routes, feeds, delay compensation, device shares and program levels are cleared to factory state; anything just restored stops at once.
wizard.inheritCleanFailed: Nothing was cleared: {{error}}. This screen is not offered to this PC twice, so try again, or switch to keeping them.

briefingPage.staged: The board still has changes waiting — go back to Routing and press the program card to make them real.
